subject: Request: 3-year price stability + uplift cap — Arcadia AI
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@arcadia.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Arcadia AI Procurement <procurement@arcadia.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: 3-year price stability (uplist cap / renewal protection)

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited. Procurement is pushing for predictable cost exposure for the platform if we move forward at scale. We are preparing a 3-year commitment but need two non-standard commercial asks to proceed with legal: (1) a price-lock (no price increases) for the first 24 months and an annual uplift cap of 8% thereafter (compounded), and (2) a renewal protection clause that allows us to renew at the prior-year blended effective rate if Redwood materially changes list pricing or introduces a materially different pricing model.

Attached is an updated SOW and a short procurement questionnaire. Can you route this for executive approval? We are targeting a signed agreement by June 10 to align with our board procurement window.

Attachments: Arcadia_SOW_v2.pdf, procurement-questions.xlsx

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Director, Strategic Procurement
Arcadia AI

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Arcadia — request for 3-year price stability (exec approval needed)

Markus / Monica — forwarding procurement request from Arcadia (see below). They want: 3-year commitment, 24-month price lock, annual uplift cap of 8% after month 24, and renewal-protection language that prevents a material downgrade on renewal.

Why I'm escalating:
- The uplift cap and renewal protection deviate from our standard escalation and indexation guardrails.
- Arcadia is a high-growth AI platform (Series C) and would bring meaningful committed spend (HubSpot deal attached).
- They are asking for a June 10 signature date.

Proposed internal guardrails if we approve:
1) Cap uplift at 9% annually (compounded) instead of 8% to balance upside and protect economics.
2) Require quarterly usage reporting and a minimum annual committed spend floor (to be defined by Monica based on their ramp).
3) Add a mutual 'material change' definition for renewal protection (e.g., >15% change in list pricing or structural changes to billing model).
4) Retain termination right for Redwood if actual consumption falls below 70% of committed volumes for two consecutive quarters.

If you both sign off, I'll communicate to Arcadia and ask legal to draft term-sheet edits (redwood-term-sheet-v3.docx).

Thanks,
Sean

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Approval: Arcadia 3-year price stability — conditional exec sign-off

Team,

After reviewing the SOW, procurement sheet, and the proposed guardrails, I authorize a conditional executive approval for Arcadia's requested structure with the following firm conditions:

1) Price lock applies for months 0–24. From month 25 onward, Redwood may apply an annual uplift not to exceed 9% (compounded).
2) Renewal protection: if Redwood materially changes list pricing or billing model, Arcadia may elect to renew at the prior-year blended effective rate for one renewal term only; 'material change' is defined as >15% absolute change in list pricing or a structural change to unitization.
3) Minimums: Arcadia must meet at least 80% of the committed annual consumption (per Monica's schedule) or trigger remediation: first notice + 60-day cure period, then prorated true-up; repeated under-performance for two consecutive quarters permits Redwood to terminate reserved capacity commitments.
4) Reporting: Arcadia will provide quarterly usage reports and enable Redwood access to usage logs for audit.
5) Legal to incorporate the language into the term sheet and prepare an execution-ready amendment for signature. No commercial credits beyond the committed discount in the term sheet without a second executive sign-off.

This approval is valid until June 25, 2026, to support the customer's June 10 internal timeline; please expedite legal.

-Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
